title: Toeplitz’s square-peg problem for arbitrary Jordan curves
open: Does every simple closed curve in the plane — no matter how wild — contain four points forming the vertices of a square? Formally, must every Jordan curve, with no smoothness, rectifiability, or finite-length assumption, inscribe a nondegenerate square?
status: Posed in 1911, the problem is settled for smooth curves and many other regularity classes. Greene–Lobb's 2026 paper establishes new Lipschitz two-graph cases. Approximation by smooth curves can produce squares collapsing to a point, so the arbitrary continuous case remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every Jordan curve in the plane contains four distinct points forming a square, with no regularity hypotheses beyond continuity and simplicity.
why: It tests whether topology alone forces a universal finite geometric pattern; the arbitrary continuous case is the last barrier to knowing whether the square-peg phenomenon is purely topological.
key_works: Joshua Evan Greene and Andrew Lobb (2021), *The rectangular peg problem*; Greene and Lobb (2026), [*Square pegs between two graphs*](https://doi.org/10.4171/CMH/619), [arXiv:2407.07798](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07798).

title: Sharp three-dimensional first-selection constant
open: Is there a point of high simplicial depth in every three-dimensional point cloud? Formally, determine the largest constant \(c_3\) such that every \(n\)-point set in general position in \(\mathbb R^3\) contains a point lying in at least \((c_3-o(1))\binom n4\) of its spanned tetrahedra; the conjectured value is \(3/32\).
status: The problem has been studied since the 1980s. Clustered constructions give the upper bound \(3/32\) in this normalization. Gromov's method and Matoušek–Wagner's refinements improve positive lower bounds without reaching that value.
solved_when: The optimal value of \(c_3\) is determined, matching the clustered-construction upper bound \(3/32\) (or refuting it with a better construction).
why: It would settle the strongest universal simplicial-depth guarantee for three-dimensional point clouds.
key_works: Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch (2010), *Stabbing simplices by points and flats*; Jiří Matoušek and Uli Wagner (2014), [*On Gromov’s method of selecting heavily covered points*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.3515).

title: Efficient refutation of sparse random 3-SAT
open: For some sufficiently large fixed constant \(c\), is there a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies unsatisfiability of a uniformly random 3-CNF formula with \(n\) variables and \(cn\) clauses with high probability, while never certifying a satisfiable formula? Alternatively, prove a computational obstruction to such refutation at constant density under a clearly stated assumption.
status: A central average-case complexity problem since the 1980s–2000s. Feige–Ofek give polynomial-time refutation at order \(n^{3/2}\) clauses; see Uriel Feige and Eran Ofek (2007), [*Easily refutable subformulas of large random 3CNF formulas*](https://doi.org/10.4086/toc.2007.v003a002), and Sarah Allen, Ryan O'Donnell and David Witmer (2015), [*How to refute a random CSP*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/random-csp-refutation.pdf). The existence of shorter certificates in sparser regimes does not imply efficient discovery of certificates at constant density.
solved_when: Either an algorithm with the above soundness and high-probability completeness guarantee exists for some fixed constant clause density \(c\), or such refutation is shown to be obstructed under a clearly stated assumption. (For context: polynomial-time refutation is currently known only from order \(n^{3/2}\) clauses.)
why: It separates efficiently recognizing typical unsatisfiability from merely proving that random formulas are almost surely unsatisfiable.
key_works: Uriel Feige and Eran Ofek (2007), [*Easily refutable subformulas of large random 3CNF formulas*](https://doi.org/10.4086/toc.2007.v003a002); Sarah Allen, Ryan O’Donnell and David Witmer (2015), [*How to refute a random CSP*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/random-csp-refutation.pdf).

title: Algorithmic threshold of the symmetric binary perceptron
open: For fixed \(\kappa>0\), what is the largest constraint density \(\alpha\) at which a polynomial-time algorithm can, with high probability, find \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \(|Gx|\le\kappa\sqrt n\) coordinatewise, where \(G\) has \(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\) independent standard-Gaussian rows?
status: The satisfiability threshold is known, but the efficient-search threshold is not. Gamarnik–Kızıldağ–Perkins–Xu (2022), [*Algorithms and Barriers in the Symmetric Binary Perceptron Model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15667), establish a multi-overlap-gap barrier for stable algorithms below the satisfiability threshold. Low-density search algorithms leave the general threshold unresolved.
solved_when: A value of \(\alpha\) is identified, matching it with either a polynomial-time algorithm achieving the above with high probability at all densities below it, or a proof that no such algorithm exists above it.
why: It provides a precise test of how the geometry of a random solution space obstructs efficient training of discrete classifiers.
key_works: David Gamarnik, Eren Kızıldağ, Will Perkins and Changji Xu (2022), [*Algorithms and Barriers in the Symmetric Binary Perceptron Model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15667).

bib.title: Algorithmic threshold of the symmetric binary perceptron

title: Unrestricted uniform sampling for the symmetric binary perceptron
open: At fixed positive density below the satisfiability threshold, can a randomized polynomial-time algorithm output an approximately uniform satisfying assignment of the symmetric binary perceptron, with total-variation error tending to zero? Settle feasibility or establish a suitable complexity-theoretic obstruction.
status: Efficient search is known to succeed at sufficiently low density. El Alaoui's 2025 theorem rules out approximate uniform sampling by stable algorithms and bounded-depth Boolean circuits at every positive density, but these restrictions do not cover all polynomial-time algorithms.
solved_when: Either a randomized polynomial-time algorithm is given that, at every fixed positive density below the satisfiability threshold, outputs a satisfying assignment whose distribution is within total-variation distance tending to zero of uniform, or a complexity-theoretic obstruction ruling out all polynomial-time samplers is proved.
why: It would determine whether efficiently found solutions can represent a typical feasible configuration.
key_works: Ahmed El Alaoui (2025), [*Hardness of Sampling Solutions From the Symmetric Binary Perceptron*](https://doi.org/10.1002/rsa.70021).

title: Infinite interchange cycles in dimensions three and four
open: Do infinite permutation cycles survive in the random interchange process on low-dimensional lattices? Formally, prove that nearest-neighbor random interchange on \(\mathbb Z^3\) and \(\mathbb Z^4\) — each edge ringing independently at rate one and swapping its endpoint labels — has infinite cycles with positive probability for all sufficiently large fixed times.
status: The problem is part of Tóth's 1993 conjecture. Elboim–Sly establish existence of infinite cycles in every dimension at least five in their 2022–2024 work [Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions, https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17023]. Numerical evidence by Barp et al. (2015) [A numerical study of the 3D random interchange and random loop models, https://doi.org/10.1088/1751-8113/48/34/345002] supports macroscopic cycles in dimension three, but the low-dimensional theorem remains open.
solved_when: The statement is proven: in each of dimensions three and four, for all sufficiently large fixed times, the random interchange permutation contains infinite cycles with positive probability.
why: It would establish a spatial permutation phase transition in exactly the dimensions where repeated encounters between random walks defeat current high-dimensional methods.
key_works: Dor Elboim and Allan Sly (2022/2024), [*Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17023); Alessandro Barp et al. (2015), [*A numerical study of the 3D random interchange and random loop models*](https://doi.org/10.1088/1751-8113/48/34/345002).

title: Roughening transition of the three-dimensional Ising interface
open: Does the standard nearest-neighbor three-dimensional Ising model have a roughening transition strictly below its bulk critical temperature? Formally, prove that the Dobrushin interface is rigid at low temperature yet delocalized in a nonempty higher-temperature regime that is still within the ordered phase.
status: The transition has been predicted for roughly half a century. Low-temperature rigidity is classical, going back to Dobrushin (1972), *Gibbs state describing coexistence of phases for a three-dimensional Ising model*. Rigorous roughening theorems exist for related solid-on-solid models, but overhangs and bubbles obstruct transferring them to the full Ising interface. A 2026 tensor-network study by Ueda, Burgelman, Tagliacozzo and Vanderstraeten, *Interface roughening in the 3-D Ising model with tensor networks* (arXiv:2601.07829), supplies further numerical evidence.
solved_when: A proof exists that the 3D nearest-neighbor Ising Dobrushin interface is localized (rigid) at sufficiently low temperature and delocalized (rough) at some intermediate temperature strictly below the bulk critical temperature, with both regimes nonempty.
why: A solution would rigorously explain how crystal facets disappear as temperature rises while bulk order survives — the mechanism by which flat facets give way to rough interfaces without losing phase coexistence.
key_works: Roland Dobrushin (1972), *Gibbs state describing coexistence of phases for a three-dimensional Ising model*; Atsushi Ueda, Lander Burgelman, Luca Tagliacozzo and Laurens Vanderstraeten (2026), [*Interface roughening in the 3-D Ising model with tensor networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07829).

title: Bounded fluctuations of planar rotor-router aggregation
open: For clockwise rotor-router aggregation on \(\mathbb Z^2\), with all rotors initially aligned and particles launched successively from the origin, is the occupied cluster after \(N\) particles within a bounded radial distance of the disk of area \(N\), uniformly in \(N\)?
status: The Euclidean limit shape is proved, and Levine–Peres establish \(O(\log r)\) fluctuations at radius \(r\) [Levine and Peres (2017), *Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits*; Levine and Peres (2009), *Strong Spherical Asymptotics for Rotor-Router Aggregation and the Divisible Sandpile*]. Simulations suggest an \(O(1)\) radial error for standard initial configurations.
solved_when: There is a constant \(C\) such that for every \(N\), the symmetric difference between the cluster of \(N\) particles and the disk of area \(N\) centered at the origin lies within radial distance \(C\) — i.e., the radial error is \(O(1)\) uniformly in \(N\).
why: It would quantify the unusually strong fluctuation suppression produced by a deterministic local rule, showing the rotor-router mechanism regularizes growth as tightly as possible.
key_works: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres (2017), [*Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.00411); Levine and Peres (2009), [*Strong Spherical Asymptotics for Rotor-Router Aggregation and the Divisible Sandpile*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11118-008-9104-6).

title: Ferrari–Spohn limit for the top SOS level line above a wall
open: Does the top macroscopic level line of the low-temperature \((2+1)\)-dimensional solid-on-solid surface in an \(L\times L\) square with zero boundary heights and a hard floor converge, near the middle of a side, to a Ferrari–Spohn diffusion? Formally, one seeks subsequences along which the fractional part of \((4\beta)^{-1}\log L\) converges away from a layering-transition value, scaling horizontally by \(L^{2/3}\) and vertically by \(L^{1/3}\), and identification of the limiting diffusion and its parameters.
status: Cube-root fluctuation bounds are known. Caddeo–Kim–Lubetzky prove a matching-order lower bound and the diffusion limit for a related setup with specially chosen boundary heights; the spontaneously selected top loop in the original box remains unresolved.
solved_when: The Ferrari–Spohn diffusion limit is proved for the top level line of the SOS surface in the original box, with horizontal scale \(L^{2/3}\) and vertical scale \(L^{1/3}\), along subsequences where the fractional part of \((4\beta)^{-1}\log L\) converges away from a layering-transition value, together with identification of the limiting diffusion and its parameters.
why: It would identify the complete fluctuation process of a random crystal facet.
key_works: Patrizio Caddeo, Yujin H. Kim and Eyal Lubetzky (2024), [*On level line fluctuations of SOS surfaces above a wall*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09106).

title: Bijective harmonious labeling of every tree
open: Does every tree admit a harmonious labeling? That is, for every \(n\)-vertex tree, is there a bijection \(f:V(T)\to\mathbb Z_n\) such that its \(n-1\) edge sums \(f(u)+f(v)\) are distinct?
status: This is part of the harmonious-labeling program originating in 1980 with Graham–Sloane, *On additive bases and harmonious graphs*. The 2025 preprint of Müyesser–Pokrovskiy, *On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture* (arXiv:2509.05280), establishes bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees; unrestricted degree patterns remain open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every \(n\)-vertex tree has a bijection to \(\mathbb Z_n\) with all \(n-1\) edge sums distinct.
why: It connects additive permutations of vertices with rainbow tree embeddings in algebraically colored complete graphs, linking the additive structure of \(\mathbb Z_n\) to extremal graph coloring questions.
key_works: Graham–Sloane (1980), *On additive bases and harmonious graphs*; Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Graham–Sloane harmonious tree conjecture
open: Is it always possible to label the vertices of a tree with \(m\) edges by the elements of \(\mathbb{Z}_m\), using every label and repeating exactly one, so that all \(m\) edge sums are distinct modulo \(m\)? Equivalently, does every tree admit a harmonious labelling in the cyclic group \(\mathbb{Z}_m\) with one permitted repeated label?
status: Proposed in 1980; verified computationally for trees through 31 vertices. Bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees are now known. Key works: Fang (2011), [*New Computational Result on Harmonious Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3490); Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every \(m\)-edge tree admits such a labelling by \(\mathbb{Z}_m\) with all \(m\) edge sums distinct modulo \(m\).
why: A positive answer would realize every element of the cyclic group exactly once as an edge sum, settling a 1980 conjecture of Graham and Sloane that sits alongside graceful labelling as a central algebraic-labelling problem for trees.
key_works: Fang (2011), [*New Computational Result on Harmonious Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3490); Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Super edge-magic tree conjecture
open: Is every finite tree super edge-magic? That is, can the vertices and edges of every \(n\)-vertex tree be labeled bijectively with \(1,\ldots,2n-1\) — vertices receiving \(1,\ldots,n\) — so that \(f(u)+f(uv)+f(v)\) is the same constant for every edge?
status: The conjecture originates with Enomoto–Lladó–Nakamigawa–Ringel (1998). It is established for caterpillars, for several additional families of trees, and for all trees through 17 vertices.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that such a bijective labeling with constant edge-sums exists for every tree on \(n\) vertices, for all \(n\).
why: It tests whether arbitrary tree structure can simultaneously support two bijectivity constraints and a rigid additive conservation rule, making it a benchmark problem at the intersection of graceful-style labelings and magic valuations.
key_works: Enomoto et al. (1998), *Super edge-magic graphs*; Ichishima–López–Muntaner-Batle–Takahashi (2022), [*Recent studies on the super edge-magic deficiency of graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.04029).

title: Faudree–Lehel irregularity-strength conjecture
open: Is there an absolute constant \(C\) such that every \(d\)-regular \(n\)-vertex graph with \(d\ge2\) admits an edge weighting by integers from \(1,\ldots,\lceil n/d\rceil+C\) whose induced weighted vertex degrees are all distinct?
status: Open since 1987 (Faudree–Lehel). Known asymptotic bounds approach \(n/d\), and Przybyło–Wei (2023) showed an additive 28 suffices in sufficiently dense degree ranges; a uniform additive constant for all degrees remains missing.
solved_when: Such an absolute constant \(C\) is exhibited (or shown not to exist), covering all \(d\)-regular \(n\)-vertex graphs with \(d\ge2\).
why: It would determine whether the elementary counting obstruction — roughly \(n/d\) distinct sums forced by the vertex count — accounts for essentially the entire labeling cost of irregularity strength.
key_works: Faudree–Lehel (1987), *Bound on the irregularity strength of regular graphs*; Przybyło–Wei (2023), [*Short Proof of the Asymptotic Confirmation of the Faudree–Lehel Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/11413).

title: Adjacent-vertex-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: Does every connected graph with at least three vertices, apart from \(C_5\), admit a proper edge coloring with \(\Delta+2\) colors in which any two adjacent vertices see different sets of incident colors?
status: Proposed by Zhang–Liu–Wang in 2002. Hatami proved a \(\Delta+300\) bound, and Joret–Lochet (2020) improved this to \(\Delta+19\) for sufficiently large maximum degree; the conjectured additive two remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that \(\Delta+2\) colors always suffice for adjacent-vertex-distinguishing proper edge colorings of every connected graph of order at least three except \(C_5\).
why: The conjecture measures exactly how much extra scheduling information beyond a proper edge coloring is needed to distinguish neighboring vertices by their incident color sets.
key_works: Zhang–Liu–Wang (2002), *Adjacent strong edge coloring of graphs*; Joret–Lochet (2020), [*Progress on the Adjacent Vertex Distinguishing Edge Coloring Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06104).

title: Proper neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: Can every graph with no isolated edge and no \(C_5\) component have its edges properly colored with the integers \(1,\ldots,\Delta+2\) so that at each vertex, the sum of incident edge colors differs from the sums at all neighboring vertices? Formally, the conjecture asserts a proper neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring with colors from \(\{1,\ldots,\Delta+2\}\) for every such graph.
status: Proposed in 2013 by Flandrin–Marczyk–Przybyło–Saclé–Woźniak in *Neighbor sum distinguishing index*. The best general asymptotic bound is \(\Delta+O(\sqrt\Delta)\). Requiring proper edge colors is what makes this a surviving problem after the 1–2–3 theorem; recent work includes Kalinowski–Pilśniak–Sidorowicz–Turowska (2026), [*Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing edge-colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01835).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the conjecture as stated: every graph without isolated edges or \(C_5\) components admits such a coloring using exactly the color set \(\{1,\ldots,\Delta+2\}\).
why: It combines conflict-free edge schedules with locally readable numerical identifiers, and after the 1–2–3 theorem it stands as one of the surviving frontiers for sum-distinguishing colorings.
key_works: Flandrin–Marczyk–Przybyło–Saclé–Woźniak (2013), *Neighbor sum distinguishing index*; Kalinowski–Pilśniak–Sidorowicz–Turowska (2026), [*Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing edge-colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01835).

title: The 1–2 total-weighting conjecture
open: Can every graph have its vertices and edges weighted with values from \(\{1,2\}\) so that adjacent vertices are always separated — that is, so that \(w(v)+\sum_{e\ni v}w(e)\) takes different values at the two ends of every edge?
status: The conjecture originates with Przybyło–Woźniak (2010), *On a 1,2 conjecture*. Deng–Qiu proved it for regular graphs in 2025; the unrestricted case remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that such a \(\{1,2\}\)-weighting exists for every graph.
why: It asks for the smallest alphabet supporting a proper vertex coloring generated entirely by additive local data, making it a fundamental test case for weighting-based coloring.
key_works: Przybyło–Woźniak (2010), *On a 1,2 conjecture*; Deng–Qiu (2025), [*The 1–2 conjecture holds for regular graphs*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0095895625000371).

title: Four locally irregular edge classes
open: If a graph admits an edge partition into locally irregular subgraphs, must four such subgraphs always suffice? Here each subgraph must be locally irregular, meaning any two adjacent vertices have different degrees within that subgraph.
status: The 2015 conjecture that three locally irregular subgraphs always suffice is false, disproved by a bow-tie counterexample; four is the revised target. Known general constant upper bounds remain above four.
solved_when: It is shown that every graph admitting any locally irregular edge decomposition can be decomposed into at most four locally irregular subgraphs — or a counterexample establishes that four does not suffice.
why: This would determine the correct universal decomposition number after the collapse of the three-class conjecture, pinning down exactly how far local irregularity can be achieved with a fixed number of colors.
key_works: Sedlar–Škrekovski (2021), [*Remarks on the Local Irregularity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08111); Grzelec–Woźniak (2022), [*On decomposing multigraphs into locally irregular submultigraphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08809).

title: Exact nonrepetitive chromatic number of the square grid
open: What is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices of the infinite square grid so that no simple path has a color sequence consisting of two consecutive identical blocks? Equivalently, determine the exact value of the nonrepetitive chromatic number of the infinite square grid.
status: Graph nonrepetitive coloring dates to around 2000, with the foundational work of Alon–Grytczuk–Hałuszczak–Riordan (2002), *Nonrepetitive colorings of graphs*. Tianyi Tao's work, published in 2026 [*The nonrepetitive coloring of grids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16237), gives bounds of five and twelve.
solved_when: The exact nonrepetitive chromatic number of the infinite square grid is determined, pinning it down between the current bounds of five and twelve.
why: A solution tests how one-dimensional repetition avoidance behaves under Cartesian products, clarifying whether the grid structure forces substantially more colors than a path.
key_works: Alon–Grytczuk–Hałuszczak–Riordan (2002), *Nonrepetitive colorings of graphs*; Tianyi Tao (2026), [*The nonrepetitive coloring of grids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16237).

bib.title: Exact nonrepetitive chromatic number of the square grid

title: Vizing’s 2-factor conjecture
open: Must every connected edge-chromatic critical graph with chromatic index \(\Delta+1\) contain a spanning 2-regular subgraph, where critical means deleting any edge lowers the chromatic index?
status: Open since the 1960s. Cases with \(\Delta\ge n/2\) are known, and further results combine degree and toughness, including toughness at least \(3/2\) together with \(\Delta\ge n/3\); see Vizing (1968), *Some unsolved problems in graph theory*, and Kanno–Shan (2019), [Vizing’s 2-Factor Conjecture Involving Toughness and Maximum Degree Conditions](https://doi.org/10.37236/7353).
solved_when: Every connected graph with chromatic index \(\Delta+1\) whose chromatic index drops upon deletion of any edge is proved to contain a spanning 2-regular subgraph, or a counterexample is exhibited.
why: It would force a spanning cycle system inside every minimal obstruction to optimal edge coloring.
key_works: Vizing (1968), *Some unsolved problems in graph theory*; Kanno–Shan (2019), [*Vizing’s 2-Factor Conjecture Involving Toughness and Maximum Degree Conditions*](https://doi.org/10.37236/7353).

title: The \(K_5\) and \(K_6\) cases of Hajós’ subdivision conjecture
open: Must every graph of chromatic number at least \(k\) contain a subdivision of \(K_k\)? This is Hajós' subdivision conjecture, unresolved at exactly the two intermediate values \(k=5\) and \(k=6\).
status: Hajós, 1961. The assertion is true through \(k=4\), false for \(k\ge7\), and unresolved at the intermediate values \(k=5\) and \(k=6\).
solved_when: A proof that every 5-chromatic graph contains a subdivision of \(K_5\), and separately, a proof that every 6-chromatic graph contains a subdivision of \(K_6\) (or a counterexample to either).
why: Resolving these last open cases would locate the exact boundary at which chromatic complexity ceases to force topological cliques, completing the picture of the conjecture from \(k=4\) to \(k\ge7\).
key_works: Catlin (1979), [*Hajós’ Graph-Coloring Conjecture: Variations and Counterexamples*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(79)90062-5); Hayashi–Kawarabayashi–Yoo (2025), [*Chasing Tripods to Obtain a Rooted Subdivision*](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M157082X).

title: Bouchet’s signed 6-flow conjecture
open: Does every flow-admissible signed graph admit a nowhere-zero integer flow with all edge values bounded in absolute value by 5? Here conservation is taken with respect to the signed incidence conventions, so negative edges reverse flow direction.
status: Proposed by Bouchet in 1983 in *Nowhere-zero integral flows on a bidirected graph*. An 11-flow theorem is known in general. Nurse's January 2026 preprint, *Bouchet's conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graphs* (arXiv:2601.05692), establishes the conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected cubic signed graphs.
solved_when: A proof that every flow-admissible signed graph has a nowhere-zero integer flow whose edge values have absolute value at most 5 (or a counterexample).
why: It would extend the classical nowhere-zero flow program to the obstructions created by negative edges, giving signed graphs the same flow structure that Tutte's conjectures provide for ordinary graphs.
key_works: Bouchet (1983), *Nowhere-zero integral flows on a bidirected graph*; Nurse (2026), [*Bouchet’s conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05692).

title: Seymour’s planar multigraph edge-coloring conjecture
open: Is every loopless planar \(r\)-regular multigraph whose odd cuts all have size at least \(r\) properly edge-colorable with \(r\) colors? Formally, must such a multigraph, satisfying \(|\delta(S)|\ge r\) for every odd-cardinality vertex set \(S\), admit a proper edge-coloring with exactly \(r\) colors?
status: Proposed in the 1970s; the cubic case is equivalent to the four-color theorem. A 2025 preprint of Chen–Naserasr establishes further cases through signed bipartite partial 3-trees and planar duality.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every loopless planar \(r\)-regular multigraph with \(|\delta(S)|\ge r\) for every odd-cardinality vertex set \(S\) is properly edge-colorable with \(r\) colors.
why: A positive answer would turn the relevant fractional matching conditions into an exact perfect-matching decomposition theorem for this class.
key_works: Chen–Naserasr (2025), [*Bounding signed bipartite partial \(t\)-trees and application to edge-coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14304).

title: Planar circular flow conjecture
open: Does every \(2k\)-edge-connected planar graph admit a circular \((2+2/k)\)-flow — that is, a conservative real flow whose edge magnitudes all lie between \(1\) and \(1+2/k\)? A positive answer would resolve the planar case of Jaeger's conjecture.
status: The conjecture is related to Jaeger's 1980s conjectures; the version for unrestricted graphs is false. For planar graphs, \(5/2\)-flows are known at edge connectivity ten, and \(7/3\)-flows at edge connectivity sixteen.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every \(2k\)-edge-connected planar graph admits a circular \((2+2/k)\)-flow for all \(k\), with edge flow magnitudes in \([1, 1+2/k]\).
why: By planar duality, the flow statement converts into sharp guarantees for circular coloring of planar graphs in terms of girth.
key_works: Jaeger (1988), *Nowhere-zero flow problems*; Cranston–Li (2020), [*Circular Flows in Planar Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.09833).

title: DeVos’ Cayley-homomorphism flow-transfer conjecture
open: If a graph homomorphism exists between the Cayley graphs \(\mathrm{Cay}(M,B)\) and \(\mathrm{Cay}(M',B')\) of finite abelian groups with symmetric connection sets, must flow existence transfer — that is, must every graph admitting a \(B\)-valued \(M\)-flow also admit a \(B'\)-valued \(M'\)-flow?
status: The conjecture was formulated by DeVos and investigated by Hušek–Šámal in 2020; a stronger proposed transfer statement is false, but the original conjecture remains open. Related work includes Hušek–Šámal (2020), [*Homomorphisms of Cayley graphs and Cycle Double Covers*](https://doi.org/10.37236/8456), and the problem connects to the finite-template promise constraint-satisfaction dichotomy problem.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that for every graph homomorphism \(\mathrm{Cay}(M,B)\to\mathrm{Cay}(M',B')\) between Cayley graphs of finite abelian groups with symmetric connection sets, every graph with a \(B\)-valued \(M\)-flow has a \(B'\)-valued \(M'\)-flow.
why: A positive answer would tie the homomorphism order on Cayley graphs to the existence of flows constrained by prescribed value sets, giving a structural bridge between two previously separate frameworks.
key_works: Hušek–Šámal (2020), [*Homomorphisms of Cayley graphs and Cycle Double Covers*](https://doi.org/10.37236/8456).

title: Three longest paths have a common vertex
open: Must every three longest paths in a connected graph share a common vertex? Formally, is there a connected graph in which three longest paths have pairwise nonempty intersection yet no single vertex lies on all three?
status: Popularized by Zamfirescu since the 1980s. Every pair of longest paths in a connected graph intersects, but Gallai's stronger question — whether one vertex is common to all longest paths — is false. Related work includes Axenovich (2009), *When do three longest paths have a common vertex?*, and Groenland–Longbrake–Steiner–Turcotte–Yepremyan (2025), [*Longest cycles in vertex-transitive and highly connected graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04618), §5.
solved_when: A proof that every three longest paths in any connected graph share a common vertex, or an explicit connected-graph counterexample.
why: This is the first unresolved Helly-type intersection condition for longest paths after the pairwise case, which is already known to hold.
key_works: Axenovich (2009), *When do three longest paths have a common vertex?*; Groenland–Longbrake–Steiner–Turcotte–Yepremyan (2025), [*Longest cycles in vertex-transitive and highly connected graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04618), §5.

title: Lovász’s path-removal conjecture
open: For every \(k\), is there a function \(f(k)\) such that every \(f(k)\)-connected graph, with any two prescribed vertices \(x\) and \(y\), contains an induced \(x\)-\(y\) path whose deletion leaves the graph \(k\)-connected?
status: Conjectured in 1975. Initial cases are solved, and Kawarabayashi–Lee–Reed–Wollan (2008) established a weaker edge-removal version of the statement; see also Chen–Gould–Yu (2003), *Graph connectivity after path removal*.
solved_when: A function \(f(k)\) is exhibited with a proof that every \(f(k)\)-connected graph and prescribed vertices \(x, y\) admit an induced \(x\)-\(y\) path whose vertex deletion leaves a \(k\)-connected graph.
why: It asks whether sufficiently robust connectivity can absorb any prescribed connecting route — whether high connectivity guarantees a "dispensable" induced path between any two vertices without destroying residual connectivity.
key_works: Chen–Gould–Yu (2003), *Graph connectivity after path removal*; Kawarabayashi et al. (2008), [*A weaker version of Lovász’ path removal conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2007.11.003).

title: Kriesell’s Steiner-tree packing conjecture
open: If every edge cut separating the terminal set \(T\) from itself has size at least \(2k\), must the graph contain \(k\) edge-disjoint trees each spanning \(T\)? Formally: does terminal edge-connectivity \(2k\) force a packing of \(k\) edge-disjoint \(T\)-Steiner trees, with nonterminal vertices allowed to be shared?
status: Proposed in 2003. DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto (2016) proved that terminal connectivity \(5k+4\) suffices for packing \(k\) Steiner trees ([*Packing Steiner Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7621)); whether the conjectured factor-two threshold holds remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that terminal connectivity \(2k\) guarantees \(k\) edge-disjoint Steiner trees spanning \(T\); the exact factor-two threshold is the target.
why: It would extend the classical spanning-tree packing theorem to networks where only a terminal subset must be connected redundantly, the natural setting for survivable network design.
key_works: DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto (2016), [*Packing Steiner Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7621).

title: Laborde–Payan–Xuong stable-set conjecture
open: Does every digraph contain an independent set of vertices that intersects every longest directed path? Equivalently, is there always a stable set that is a transversal for the collection of maximum-length directed paths?
status: Proposed in 1983 by Laborde, Payan, and Xuong. Havet (2004) proved the conjecture for digraphs with independence number at most two; further structured classes of digraphs are also known to satisfy it.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for all finite digraphs: either every digraph admits an independent vertex set meeting every longest directed path, or a digraph is exhibited in which no independent set intersects all longest directed paths.
why: It would establish a strong structural relationship between independent sets and extremal directed paths in digraphs, the directed analogue of classical path–transversal phenomena for undirected graphs.
key_works: Laborde–Payan–Xuong (1983), *Independent sets and longest directed paths in digraphs*; Havet (2004), *Stable set meeting every longest path*, and [author’s problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/stable_set_meeting_all_longest_directed_paths).

title: Bang-Jensen–Yeo strong spanning decomposition conjecture
open: Is there an absolute constant \(k\) such that every \(k\)-arc-connected digraph contains two arc-disjoint strongly connected spanning subdigraphs? Formally, does sufficiently high arc-connectivity alone force such a decomposition into two spanning strongly connected networks?
status: The conjecture was formulated in 2004 by Bang-Jensen–Yeo (*Decomposing \(k\)-arc-strong tournaments into strong spanning subdigraphs*). The existence assertion holds for tournaments and other special classes, but it remains open for general digraphs; the problem is also recorded in Havet's [research problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/arc_disjoint_strongly_connected_spanning_subdigraphs).
solved_when: A specific integer \(k\) is exhibited (with proof) such that every \(k\)-arc-connected digraph admits two arc-disjoint strongly connected spanning subdigraphs.
why: It asks whether sufficiently redundant directed connectivity always separates into two independently functioning spanning networks, a basic structural guarantee for fault-tolerant directed designs.
key_works: Bang-Jensen–Yeo (2004), *Decomposing \(k\)-arc-strong tournaments into strong spanning subdigraphs*; Havet’s [research problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/arc_disjoint_strongly_connected_spanning_subdigraphs).

title: Linear Ramsey growth for hypercubes
open: Is the Ramsey number of the $d$-dimensional hypercube at most a constant multiple of its vertex count — that is, does $R(Q_d)\le C2^d$ hold for an absolute constant $C$?
status: The question dates to Burr and Erdős in the 1970s (Burr–Erdős, 1975, *On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs*). The best known result, due to Tikhomirov (2024, [*A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14568)), is $R(Q_d)=O(2^{(2-c)d})$ with $c=0.03656$ permissible. The conjectured exponent of one remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the bound $R(Q_d)\le C2^d$ for an absolute constant $C$; equivalently, showing the exponential rate is exactly one, $R(Q_d)=2^{(1+o(1))d}$.
why: It tests whether the high symmetry of the hypercube can keep Ramsey growth linear in the number of vertices despite its unbounded maximum degree, in the spirit of the Burr–Erdős conjecture for bounded-degree/sparse graphs.
key_works: Burr–Erdős (1975), *On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs*; Tikhomirov (2024), [*A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14568).

title: Exact value of \(R(3,10)\)
open: Is the Ramsey number \(R(3,10)\) equal to 40 or to 41? Equivalently, does there exist a triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with independence number at most nine?
status: This is the first unresolved entry of the classical \(R(3,t)\) sequence. The lower bound is 40, and Angeltveit (2024) proves the upper bound \(R(3,10)\le 41\).
solved_when: The exact value of \(R(3,10)\) is determined: either a triangle-free 40-vertex graph with independence number at most nine is exhibited (proving \(R(3,10)=41\)), or it is certified that no such graph exists (proving \(R(3,10)=40\)).
why: As the first unresolved entry of the classical \(R(3,t)\) sequence, this value is a sharply bounded frontier for exhaustive graph classification and certified nonexistence proofs.
key_works: Exoo (1989), *On two classical Ramsey numbers*; Angeltveit (2024), [*\(R(3,10)\le41\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00392).

title: Exponential dependence on maximum degree in Ramsey’s theorem
open: Is there an absolute constant \(C\) such that every \(n\)-vertex graph of maximum degree \(\Delta\) has Ramsey number \(R(H)\le 2^{C\Delta}n\)? In other words, is exponential dependence on \(\Delta\) — with no extra logarithmic factor — sufficient for linearity in \(n\)?
status: Linearity of Ramsey numbers for bounded-degree graphs dates to Chvátal–Rödl–Szemerédi–Trotter (1983), *The Ramsey number of a graph with bounded maximum degree*. Exponential dependence on \(\Delta\) is necessary, but the best general upper bound, due to Conlon–Fox–Sudakov (2012), [*On two problems in graph Ramsey theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0045), is \(2^{O(\Delta\log\Delta)}n\), retaining an extra logarithm.
solved_when: A proof of \(R(H)\le 2^{C\Delta}n\) for every \(n\)-vertex graph \(H\) of maximum degree \(\Delta\), with an absolute constant \(C\).
why: It would determine the correct degree penalty in sparse Ramsey theory, since exponential dependence on \(\Delta\) is known to be necessary while current bounds carry an extra logarithmic factor.
key_works: Chvátal–Rödl–Szemerédi–Trotter (1983), *The Ramsey number of a graph with bounded maximum degree*; Conlon–Fox–Sudakov (2012), [*On two problems in graph Ramsey theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0045).

title: Growth of the generalized Ramsey function \(f(n,4,3)\)
open: How many colors are needed to edge-color \(K_n\) so that every four vertices span at least three distinct colors? Formally, determine the order of growth of the generalized Ramsey function \(f(n,4,3)\).
status: Part of the Erdős–Gyárfás program on generalized Ramsey numbers. The best known bounds leave \(f(n,4,3)\) between \(\Omega(\log n)\) and \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))\).
solved_when: The order of \(f(n,4,3)\) is determined up to constant factors in the exponent — i.e., matching upper and lower bounds are established, closing the current gap between \(\Omega(\log n)\) and \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))\).
why: It captures an intermediate regime of the Erdős–Gyárfás program between avoiding monochromatic cliques and requiring locally diverse colorings, and resolving it would clarify where local color-diversity demands stop being cheap.
key_works: Erdős–Gyárfás (1997), *A variant of the classical Ramsey problem*; Mubayi (1998), *Edge-coloring cliques with three colors on all 4-cliques*; Conlon–Fox–Lee–Sudakov (2015), [*The Erdős–Gyárfás problem on generalized Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0250).

title: Ordinary Turán density of the broken tetrahedron
open: Is the ordinary Turán density of the broken tetrahedron — the 3-uniform hypergraph \(K_4^{(3)-}\) consisting of three triples on four vertices — equal to \(2/7\)? In other words, does the Frankl–Füredi construction, which achieves density \(2/7\), actually attain the true extremal value?
status: Frankl–Füredi constructions give \(2/7\); upper bounds remain slightly larger. The ordinary density remains open, despite solved codegree and uniform-density variants.
solved_when: \(\pi(K_4^{(3)-})\) is determined exactly; the conjectured value is \(2/7\), so success means proving the matching upper bound \(\pi(K_4^{(3)-}) \le 2/7\).
why: This is one of the smallest hypergraphs whose extremal density is still unknown, making it a basic missing case in extremal hypergraph theory.
key_works: Frankl–Füredi (1984), *An exact result for 3-graphs*; Falgas-Ravry–Pikhurko–Vaughan–Volec (2023), [*The codegree threshold of \(K_4^-\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09396); Piga–Schülke (2026), [*Hypergraphs with arbitrarily small codegree Turán density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02876).

bib.title: Ordinary Turán density of the broken tetrahedron

title: Extremal number of the cube graph
open: What is the true asymptotic order of the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of the cube graph $Q_3$? Equivalently, determine the asymptotic behavior of $\operatorname{ex}(n,Q_3)$, whose exponent is currently only known to lie between $3/2$ and $8/5$.
status: Erdős–Simonovits proved the upper bound $O(n^{8/5})$ in 1970, while $C_4$-free constructions give a lower bound of $\Omega(n^{3/2})$; the exponent remains unsettled. Key works include Erdős–Simonovits (1970), *Some extremal problems in graph theory*; the [author problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TuranCube.html); and Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).
solved_when: The asymptotic order of $\operatorname{ex}(n,Q_3)$ is determined up to a constant factor; in particular, the exponent is pinned down — either $n^{3/2}$, $n^{8/5}$, or some intermediate value is settled, with matching upper and lower bounds.
why: The cube is a small, highly symmetric bipartite graph, yet the standard extremal toolbox still leaves an exponent gap of $3/2$ versus $8/5$; resolving it would reveal which methods genuinely control degenerate Turán problems at this boundary.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1970), *Some extremal problems in graph theory*; [author problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TuranCube.html); Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

bib.title: Extremal number of the cube graph

title: Erdős–Simonovits odd-cycle compactness
open: For every finite family \(\mathcal F\) of bipartite graphs, does forbidding \(\mathcal F\) together with all sufficiently short odd cycles recover, asymptotically, the extremal number of \(\mathcal F\)-free bipartite graphs? Formally, is there a bound \(L\) such that graphs containing no member of \(\mathcal F\) and no odd cycle of length at most \(L\) have asymptotically the same extremal number as \(\mathcal F\)-free bipartite graphs?
status: Proposed in 1982 by Erdős–Simonovits in *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*. Strong versions are proved for smooth bipartite families, including several complete bipartite cases (Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte, 2014, *Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*); the question for arbitrary finite families remains open.
solved_when: For every finite family \(\mathcal F\) of bipartite graphs, an \(L = L(\mathcal F)\) is exhibited such that the extremal number of graphs forbidding \(\mathcal F\) and all odd cycles of length at most \(L\) is asymptotically equal to that of \(\mathcal F\)-free bipartite graphs.
why: It asks whether finitely many odd-cycle exclusions can reproduce a global bipartiteness constraint — a compactness phenomenon for extremal graph theory, showing local forbidden subgraph conditions suffice for the bipartite extremal structure.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1982), *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*; Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

title: Tuza’s saturation-limit conjecture
open: For every fixed graph \(F\) with an edge, does \(\operatorname{sat}(n,F)/n\) converge? Here saturation means \(F\)-free, but adding any missing edge creates \(F\).
status: Tuza, 1986. Calbet–Freschi’s 2026 paper repairs a gap in a classical partial theorem. Finite forbidden families can have nonconvergent ratios; the singleton case remains open.
why: Would establish a stable asymptotic density for minimal saturation.
key_works: Calbet–Freschi (2026), [*The Asymptotic Behaviour of \(\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10847).

title: Subdivision exponent-halving conjecture
open: If a fixed bipartite graph \(F\) has extremal number \(\operatorname{ex}(n,F)=O(n^{1+\alpha})\), must its one-subdivision \(\operatorname{sub}(F)\), obtained by subdividing every edge exactly once, satisfy \(\operatorname{ex}(n,\operatorname{sub}(F))=O(n^{1+\alpha/2})\)?
status: The predicted behavior is established for subdivisions of complete bipartite graphs (Kang–Kim–Liu, 2018), but the universal implication remains open. Key works: Kang–Kim–Liu (2021), [*On the rational Turán exponents conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06916); Conlon–Janzer–Lee (2021), [*More on the extremal number of subdivisions*](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/sqbep-vc039).
solved_when: A proof, or a counterexample, of the implication: for every fixed bipartite \(F\) with \(\operatorname{ex}(n,F)=O(n^{1+\alpha})\), the bound \(\operatorname{ex}(n,\operatorname{sub}(F))=O(n^{1+\alpha/2})\) holds, where every edge of \(F\) is subdivided once.
why: It would give a general transformation law for Turán exponents under subdivision, allowing extremal numbers of subdivisions to be read off from those of the original bipartite graphs.
key_works: Kang–Kim–Liu (2021), [*On the rational Turán exponents conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06916); Conlon–Janzer–Lee (2021), [*More on the extremal number of subdivisions*](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/sqbep-vc039).

title: Linear density of \(k\)-quasiplanar graphs
open: For every fixed \(k\), must every \(n\)-vertex topological graph with no \(k\) pairwise crossing edges have at most \(C_k n\) edges — that is, is the edge count linear in \(n\) with a constant depending only on \(k\)?
status: Conjectured in the 1990s. Linear bounds hold for small \(k\); general bounds retain logarithmic or slightly larger factors, as in Fox–Pach–Suk (2013), [*The number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2361), and Suk–Walczak (2016), [*New bounds on the maximum number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0395).
solved_when: For each fixed \(k\), there exists a constant \(C_k\) such that every \(n\)-vertex topological graph with no \(k\) pairwise crossing edges has at most \(C_k n\) edges.
why: It tests whether excluding a fixed crossing clique controls density almost as strongly as planarity itself.
key_works: Fox–Pach–Suk (2013), [*The number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2361); Suk–Walczak (2016), [*New bounds on the maximum number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0395).

title: Sharp star chromatic number of planar graphs
open: What is the smallest number of colors needed to color every planar graph so that the coloring is proper and no path on four vertices alternates between just two colors? Equivalently, determine the sharp value of the star chromatic number of planar graphs.
status: Albertson and collaborators proved \(10\le C\le20\) in 2004; the general planar gap remains open. Key works: Albertson–Chappell–Kierstead–Kündgen–Ramamurthi (2004), [*Coloring with no 2-colored \(P_4\)’s*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1779); West, [*Star colorings and acyclic colorings*](https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/starcol.html).
solved_when: The exact smallest \(C\) is determined such that every planar graph admits a proper vertex coloring with \(C\) colors and no bichromatic four-vertex path, closing the gap between the known bounds \(10\le C\le20\).
why: It pins down the exact cost, in colors, of requiring every pair of color classes to induce a star forest, a structural constraint central to star and acyclic coloring.
key_works: Albertson–Chappell–Kierstead–Kündgen–Ramamurthi (2004), [*Coloring with no 2-colored \(P_4\)’s*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1779); West, [*Star colorings and acyclic colorings*](https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/starcol.html).

title: A positive Schur rule for arbitrary LLT polynomials
open: Is there a uniform combinatorial rule, with nonnegative \(q\)-weights, that gives every Schur coefficient of any LLT polynomial indexed by an arbitrary tuple of skew diagrams?
status: Algebraic Schur positivity is known. Direct coefficient rules exist only for restricted shapes and graph families; a positive rule in the unrestricted setting remains missing (see Lascoux–Leclerc–Thibon, 1997, *Ribbon tableaux, Hall–Littlewood functions, quantum affine algebras, and unipotent varieties*; Wang, 2025, [Expanding the unicellular LLT polynomials of two-headed melting lollipops into ribbon Schurs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08187)).
solved_when: A rule is exhibited that, for LLT polynomials indexed by an arbitrary tuple of skew diagrams, expresses each Schur coefficient as a nonnegative \(q\)-weighted count of combinatorial objects.
why: Such a rule could explain substantial parts of Macdonald positivity and improve computation of the coefficients.
key_works: Lascoux–Leclerc–Thibon (1997), *Ribbon tableaux, Hall–Littlewood functions, quantum affine algebras, and unipotent varieties* (verify); Wang (2025), [*Expanding the unicellular LLT polynomials of two-headed melting lollipops into ribbon Schurs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08187).

bib.title: A positive Schur rule for arbitrary LLT polynomials

title: Schur positivity of Macdonald cumulants
open: Are Macdonald cumulants Schur positive? That is, when a Macdonald cumulant is expanded in the Schur basis, are all coefficients nonnegative?
status: Dołęga (2017) established polynomiality, monomial and fundamental positivity, and positivity of hook Schur coefficients; full Schur positivity remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with explicit counterexample) of Schur positivity of Macdonald cumulants is given.
why: A positive answer would isolate the connected contributions concealed inside individual Macdonald polynomials, separating them from the rest of the expansion.
key_works: Dołęga (2017), [*Macdonald cumulants, \(G\)-inversion polynomials and \(G\)-parking functions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02656).

title: Schur positivity of LLT cumulants
open: Is every LLT cumulant of a colored tuple of skew shapes, in Dołęga–Kowalski's normalization, Schur positive — that is, does it expand in the Schur basis with coefficients in \(\mathbb N[q]\)?
status: The conjecture was made in 2022 by Dołęga and Kowalski in [*LLT Cumulants and Graph Coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12676), [journal version](https://doi.org/10.37236/10977). Currently established: monomial and fundamental positivity, positivity of hook coefficients, results for vertical shapes, and the case of melting lollipops.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) that every LLT cumulant of every colored tuple of skew shapes has Schur coefficients in \(\mathbb N[q]\).
why: Schur positivity of LLT cumulants would imply Schur positivity of Macdonald cumulants via a positive expansion, resolving a major positivity question in symmetric function theory.
key_works: Dołęga–Kowalski (2022), [*LLT Cumulants and Graph Coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12676), [journal version](https://doi.org/10.37236/10977).

title: Goulden–Jackson Matchings–Jack positivity
open: Are the Jack connection coefficients \(c_{\mu,\nu}^{\lambda}(1+b)\), taken in the triple-Cauchy normalization, always polynomials in \(b\) with nonnegative integer coefficients — and if so, is there a nonnegative statistic on matchings that explains this positivity?
status: Open since 1996. Polynomiality of the coefficients is known, positivity has been established for the top-degree part (Burchardt, 2021), and further labeled cases were established in 2024.
solved_when: A proof that \(c_{\mu,\nu}^{\lambda}(1+b) \in \mathbb{N}[b]\) for all partitions \(\mu, \nu, \lambda\), together with a combinatorial (nonnegative) statistic on matchings whose enumeration yields these coefficients.
why: It would explain the interpolation between the symmetric-group class algebra and the double-coset algebra, giving a uniform combinatorial meaning to the whole family of connection coefficients.
key_works: Goulden–Jackson (1996), [*Connection coefficients, matchings, maps and combinatorial conjectures for Jack symmetric functions*](https://uwaterloo.ca/math/sites/default/files/uploads/documents/gjtams1996.pdf); Burchardt (2021), [*The Top-Degree Part in the Matchings-Jack Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09330).

title: Falling-factorial positivity for shifted Jack polynomials
open: Is the shifted Jack polynomial, after a suitable rescaling by a power of the Jack parameter, always a nonnegative combination of falling factorials? Formally: prove that \(\alpha^{\ell(\mu)-1}H_\mu P_\mu^\#(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) has nonnegative coefficients when expanded in the falling-factorial basis.
status: Alexandersson–Féray (2017) established computational evidence and special cases; no general shifted Knop–Sahi-type combinatorial rule is known.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the nonnegativity of the falling-factorial expansion of \(\alpha^{\ell(\mu)-1}H_\mu P_\mu^\#(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) for arbitrary partitions \(\mu\); no quantitative parameters beyond this appear in the record.
why: A proof would explain the observed positivity of these polynomials at partition arguments and support positive multiplication recurrences.
key_works: Alexandersson–Féray (2017), [*Shifted symmetric functions and multirectangular coordinates of Young diagrams*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.02447).

bib.title: Falling-factorial positivity for shifted Jack polynomials

title: Thrall’s higher Lie multiplicity problem
open: Is there a positive, Littlewood–Richardson-type multiplicity rule for the Schur expansion of every higher Lie module \(\mathcal L_\lambda=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{m_i}(\mathcal L_i)\), where \(m_i\) counts the parts of size \(i\) in \(\lambda\) and \(\mathcal L_i\) is the degree-\(i\) free Lie module?
status: The problem originates with Thrall (1942). Individual homogeneous free Lie pieces are understood through a major-index rule (Armon–Swanson 2025, *Super major index and Thrall's problem*, https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.421), and the asymptotics of higher Lie characters have been studied (Adin–Roichman–Tsilevich 2025, *Asymptotics of higher Lie characters*, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.12904), but arbitrary higher products remain unresolved.
solved_when: A combinatorial (positive) rule is given that computes \([\,S_\mu : \mathcal L_\lambda\,]\) as a count of explicit tableaux-type objects for every partition \(\lambda\).
why: Such a rule would explain the PBW (Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt) decomposition of the tensor algebra at the level of irreducible representations, showing exactly which Schur constituents occur and with what multiplicity.
key_works: Armon–Swanson (2025), [*Super major index and Thrall’s problem*](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.421); Adin–Roichman–Tsilevich (2025), [*Asymptotics of higher Lie characters*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.12904).

title: Macdonald filling conjugation exchanging inversion and major index
open: Is there a content-preserving bijection from fillings of a partition shape \(\mu\) to fillings of the conjugate shape \(\mu'\) that exchanges the Haglund–Haiman–Loehr statistics \(\operatorname{inv}\) and \(\operatorname{maj}\)?
status: The underlying polynomial identity is proved. Bijections exist for hook shapes and specialized cases, but the general construction remains open; see Haglund–Haiman–Loehr (2005), *A combinatorial formula for Macdonald polynomials*, and Gillespie–Kaliszewski–Morse (2016), [*Macdonald symmetry at \(q=1\) and a new class of inv-preserving bijections on words*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.04973).
solved_when: An explicit such bijection is constructed and proved to preserve content and send \(\operatorname{inv}\) to \(\operatorname{maj}\) and \(\operatorname{maj}\) to \(\operatorname{inv}\) for arbitrary shapes.
why: It would directly explain the conjugate-shape symmetry between the two local statistics, turning the known polynomial identity into structural combinatorial understanding.
key_works: Haglund–Haiman–Loehr (2005), *A combinatorial formula for Macdonald polynomials*; Gillespie–Kaliszewski–Morse (2016), [*Macdonald symmetry at \(q=1\) and a new class of inv-preserving bijections on words*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.04973).

bib.title: Macdonald filling conjugation exchanging inversion and major index

title: Content-preserving parking-function \(q,t\)-symmetry
open: Is there an explicit bijection on word parking functions that preserves label content and exchanges the statistics area and dinv? Such a map would realize, object by object and for every fixed content, the symmetry known to hold at the level of generating functions.
status: The shuffle theorem establishes the generating-function equality, but a uniform bijection remains open; the labeled problem strengthens the known unlabelled \(q,t\)-Catalan symmetry. Key works: Carlsson–Mellit (2018), *A proof of the shuffle conjecture*; Gillespie (2020), [*Two \(q,t\)-symmetry problems in symmetric function theory*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/01/12/two-qt-symmetry-problems-in-symmetric-function-theory/), OPAC-029.
solved_when: A uniform, explicit bijection is constructed on word parking functions that, for every content, fixes the label content and interchanges area with dinv.
why: It would expose the symmetry of diagonal coinvariant rings directly on their combinatorial objects, rather than only through symmetric-function identities.
key_works: Carlsson–Mellit (2018), *A proof of the shuffle conjecture*; Gillespie (2020), [*Two \(q,t\)-symmetry problems in symmetric function theory*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/01/12/two-qt-symmetry-problems-in-symmetric-function-theory/), OPAC-029.

title: Asymptotic sign balance in symmetric-group character tables
open: Among the nonzero irreducible character-table entries of \(S_n\), does the proportion that are positive tend to \(1/2\) as \(n\) grows? Equivalently, is the conditional distribution of signs, given a nonzero entry, asymptotically balanced between positive and negative?
status: Miller's 2017 computations suggest this balance. Hopkins's 2025 discussion retains the question; existing zero-density and divisibility results do not determine the conditional sign distribution.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that the proportion of positive entries among nonzero irreducible character values of \(S_n\) tends to \(1/2\) as \(n \to \infty\).
why: It would establish a global cancellation law in one of the most fundamental families of representation-theoretic data, revealing structure that pointwise zero-density and divisibility results cannot see.
key_works: Miller (2017), [*Note on parity and the irreducible characters of the symmetric group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.03267); Hopkins (2025), [*Maximizing negative entries in symmetric group character tables*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2025/05/02/maximizing-negative-entries-in-symmetric-group-character-tables/).

bib.title: Asymptotic sign balance in symmetric-group character tables

title: Schur positivity of monomial immanants of Jacobi–Trudi matrices
open: Is every monomial immanant of a Jacobi–Trudi matrix a Schur-positive symmetric function? That is, when the determinant of a Jacobi–Trudi matrix is twisted by a monomial character of the symmetric group, do the resulting coefficients in the Schur basis all come out nonnegative?
status: The assertion is Stembridge's 1992 conjecture and remains open as listed in Shareshian–Wachs's 2026 survey; known results for ordinary irreducible-character immanants do not establish the monomial case. Key works: Haiman (1993), *Hecke algebra characters and immanant conjectures*; Shareshian–Wachs (2026), *Combinatorics and Hessenberg varieties*.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that every monomial immanant of every Jacobi–Trudi matrix expands in the Schur basis with nonnegative coefficients.
why: A proof would forge a concrete bridge between total positivity, Hecke algebra characters, and Hessenberg geometry, explaining the positivity phenomenon uniformly rather than case by case.
key_works: Haiman (1993), [*Hecke algebra characters and immanant conjectures*](https://web.math.berkeley.edu/~mhaiman/ftp/heckeimm/jams1.pdf); Shareshian–Wachs (2026), [*Combinatorics and Hessenberg varieties*](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003145127-9).

bib.title: Schur positivity of monomial immanants of Jacobi–Trudi matrices

title: Enumeration of the type-\(B\) Bruhat completion
open: How many elements does the Bruhat–MacNeille completion of the type-\(B\) Coxeter group \(B_n\) have? More precisely, find a uniform formula, a recurrence, or an effectively computable generating function for this number as a function of \(n\).
status: The initial counts \(2, 10, 132, 4824\) are known for \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4\); beyond these, the enumeration remains open independently of any structural model. Relevant background appears in Geck–Kim (1997), *Bases for the Bruhat–Chevalley order on all finite Coxeter groups*, and Hopkins (2022), [*The Dedekind–MacNeille completion of type B Bruhat order*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2022/08/02/the-dedekind-macneille-completion-of-type-b-bruhat-order/).
solved_when: A closed formula, recurrence, or effectively solvable generating function is established that reproduces the known values \(2, 10, 132, 4824\) for \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4\) and yields the count for all \(n\).
why: A solution could reveal an integrable symmetry class of alternating sign matrices or expose an entirely new enumerative structure underlying the type-\(B\) Bruhat order.
key_works: Geck–Kim (1997), *Bases for the Bruhat–Chevalley order on all finite Coxeter groups*; Hopkins (2022), [*The Dedekind–MacNeille completion of type B Bruhat order*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2022/08/02/the-dedekind-macneille-completion-of-type-b-bruhat-order/).

bib.title: Enumeration of the type-\(B\) Bruhat completion

title: Strong Sperner property for finite Coxeter weak orders
open: Is the weak order of every finite Coxeter group strongly Sperner — that is, does the largest union of \(k\) antichains always have size equal to the sum of the \(k\) largest ranks? A positive answer would extend the classical Sperner property to all \(k\) simultaneously across reflection-group orders.
status: Gaetz–Gao (2020), [*A combinatorial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-action and the Sperner property for the weak order*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05501), settle type \(A\) via a combinatorial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-action. The extension to all finite Coxeter groups remains conjectural.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for every finite Coxeter group that the maximum size of a union of \(k\) antichains in the weak order equals the sum of the \(k\) largest ranks, for all \(k\).
why: It would determine sharp extremal bounds for incomparable collections throughout reflection-group orders.
key_works: Gaetz–Gao (2020), [*A combinatorial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-action and the Sperner property for the weak order*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05501).

bib.title: Strong Sperner property for finite Coxeter weak orders

title: Dyer’s complete-lattice conjecture for extended weak order
open: Is the poset of biclosed subsets of the positive real roots, ordered by inclusion, a complete lattice for every Coxeter group? Here a subset of positive real roots is biclosed when both it and its complement contain every positive root lying in the nonnegative span of two of its roots.
status: The conjecture is established for finite Coxeter groups (Dyer, 2019, [On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5557)) and for affine Coxeter groups (Barkley–Speyer, 2023, revised 2025, [Affine extended weak order is a lattice](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737)); general indefinite Coxeter systems remain open.
solved_when: The inclusion poset of biclosed subsets of the positive real roots is proven to be a complete lattice for arbitrary Coxeter systems, including the indefinite case.
why: A positive answer extends weak-order lattice operations — joins and meets — from finite Coxeter groups to infinite reflection groups.
key_works: Dyer (2019), [*On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5557); Barkley–Speyer (2023, revised 2025), [*Affine extended weak order is a lattice*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737).

title: Dyer’s maximal-chain conjecture for biclosed sets
open: Does every maximal chain in the extended weak order arise in the canonical way — that is, as the sequence of initial segments of a unique total ordering of the positive roots?
status: This is Dyer's Conjecture A. The conjecture is known for finite Coxeter groups and for affine Coxeter groups; the unrestricted indefinite case remains open. See Dyer (2019), *On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups*, and Barkley–Speyer (2023, revised 2025), [*Affine extended weak order is a lattice*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737), Conjecture 1.2 and Theorem D.
solved_when: It is proved that every maximal chain in the extended weak order (with no restriction on the Coxeter group, including the indefinite case) consists exactly of the initial segments of a unique total order on the positive roots.
why: A positive answer would identify maximal inversion chains with coherent root enumerations, tying the structure of the extended weak order directly to ordered listings of positive roots.
key_works: Dyer (2019), *On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups*; Barkley–Speyer (2023, revised 2025), [*Affine extended weak order is a lattice*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737), Conjecture 1.2 and Theorem D.

title: Log-concavity of \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials
open: For every finite labeled poset \(P\), is the \(P\)-Eulerian polynomial \(\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal L(P)}t^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}\) log-concave with no internal zeros? Equivalently, does the descent distribution over the linear extensions of any labeled poset form a log-concave sequence?
status: Brenti's conjecture survives counterexamples to Negers–Stanley real-rootedness. Alexandersson–Jal (2024–2026) establish stronger log-concavity for naturally labeled width-two posets [*Rook matroids and log-concavity of \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials*, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00127]. Foundational background: Brenti (1989), *Unimodal, log-concave and Pólya frequency sequences in combinatorics*.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every finite labeled poset \(P\), the coefficients of \(\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal L(P)}t^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}\) form a log-concave sequence with no internal zeros.
why: It would recover a robust distributional regularity for \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials after the stronger real-rootedness prediction (Negers–Stanley) failed, restoring the structural picture Brenti's conjecture was meant to provide.
key_works: Brenti (1989), *Unimodal, log-concave and Pólya frequency sequences in combinatorics*; Alexandersson–Jal (2024–2026), [*Rook matroids and log-concavity of \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00127).

title: Central zonotopal algebras determine bridge-free graphic matroids
open: Do the central zonotopal algebras of two connected loopless graphs coincide exactly when the graphs agree up to their cycle matroids, once bridges are deleted? Precisely, prove that isomorphism of the central zonotopal algebras is equivalent to isomorphism of the bridge-deleted cycle matroids.
status: Nenashev classified the external analogue in 2019. The central equivalence remains open; its Hilbert series alone is insufficient.
solved_when: The equivalence is proved: two connected loopless graphs have isomorphic central zonotopal algebras if and only if their cycle matroids are isomorphic after deleting all bridges.
why: It would determine exactly how much graph structure survives in a natural finite-dimensional cut-power algebra, showing the algebra forgets precisely the bridges and nothing more.
key_works: Nenashev (2019), *Classification of external zonotopal algebras*; Nenashev (2020), [*Isomorphisms of zonotopal algebras*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/03/08/isomorphisms-of-zonotopal-algebras/), OPAC-032.

title: Isomorphism classification of internal zonotopal algebras
open: When do two connected graphs give rise to isomorphic internal zonotopal algebras, those built from cut powers with exponent \(d_I-1\)? The goal is a necessary and sufficient combinatorial characterization in terms of the graphs themselves.
status: The problem is explicitly open in Nenashev's 2020 problem list (Nenashev 2020, [Isomorphisms of zonotopal algebras](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/03/08/isomorphisms-of-zonotopal-algebras/)). The external zonotopal algebras are classified, but no comparable isomorphism criterion exists for the internal case. Foundational background appears in Ardila–Postnikov (2010), [Combinatorics and geometry of power ideals](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-10-05018-X).
solved_when: A checkable combinatorial condition on connected graphs is given, proved to hold exactly when their internal zonotopal algebras (defined via cut powers with exponent \(d_I-1\)) are isomorphic.
why: A solution would identify which graph structures can be reconstructed from their interior-enumeration algebras.
key_works: Ardila–Postnikov (2010), [*Combinatorics and geometry of power ideals*](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-10-05018-X); Nenashev (2020), [*Isomorphisms of zonotopal algebras*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/03/08/isomorphisms-of-zonotopal-algebras/).

title: The exact universal matroid correlation constant
open: What is the largest positive correlation that the rank function of a matroid can exhibit, in a universal sense across all matroids? Formally, determine the exact supremum of the universal matroid correlation constant.
status: Huh–Schröter–Wang prove bounds 8/7 and 2. The exact worst positive correlation remains unknown.
solved_when: The exact value of the supremum is determined (identified and proved), improving on the known bounds of 8/7 and 2.
why: It quantifies how far matroid rank functions can depart from the spanning-tree-like negative dependence behavior, sharpening our understanding of correlation structure in matroids.
key_works: Huh–Schröter–Wang (2018), [*Correlation bounds for fields and matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02675).

title: Does matroid correlation depend on the representation field?
open: Does the correlation exponent for representable matroids depend on the choice of the representation field? In particular, is the conjectured value \(\alpha_{\mathbb F_2}=8/7\) correct?
status: The bounds \(8/7\le\alpha_{\mathbb F}\le2\) hold for every field; characteristic and field-size dependence remain undetermined. See Huh–Schröter–Wang (2018), [*Correlation bounds for fields and matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02675).
solved_when: The quantity \(\alpha_{\mathbb F}\) (the relevant supremum restricted to \(\mathbb F\)-representable matroids) is shown to either be field-independent for all fields, or a specific pair of fields is exhibited for which it differs; the specific value \(\alpha_{\mathbb F_2}=8/7\) is proved or refuted.
why: A separation between fields would reveal probabilistic information about representability that is invisible to current techniques.
key_works: Huh–Schröter–Wang (2018), [*Correlation bounds for fields and matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02675).

title: A complete excluded-minor list for \(GF(5)\)-representability
open: Which matroids are minor-minimal obstructions to representability over the five-element field, and can the full list be given with a proof that it is complete?
status: Unlike the binary, ternary, and quaternary classifications, the quinary classification remains unfinished. Brettell (2025), [*The excluded minors for \(GF(5)\)-representable matroids on ten elements*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14614), finds 2,128 ten-element excluded minors, supplementing 564 on at most nine elements ([computation resources](https://homepages.ecs.vuw.ac.nz/~bretteni/research.html)).
solved_when: Every minor-minimal matroid not representable over \(GF(5)\) is determined, together with a completeness proof; this includes the 2,128 ten-element excluded minors and the 564 on at most nine elements already found.
why: A solution would turn quinary representability into a concrete finite obstruction theorem, on par with the binary, ternary, and quaternary classifications.
key_works: Brettell (2025), [*The excluded minors for \(GF(5)\)-representable matroids on ten elements*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14614), [computation resources](https://homepages.ecs.vuw.ac.nz/~bretteni/research.html).

title: Complete excluded minors for dyadic matroids
open: Which finite set of matroids forms the complete list of excluded minors for the class of matroids representable over both GF(3) and GF(5)? Formally, determine every minor-minimal matroid not representable over both of these fields.
status: Brettell–Pendavingh (2024), in [*Computing Excluded Minors for Classes of Matroids Representable over Partial Fields*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13175), enumerate the excluded minors through fifteen elements and exhibit a sixteen-element obstruction; this is not yet a complete classification.
solved_when: A complete classification of all excluded minors for the class of matroids representable over both GF(3) and GF(5) is given — including deciding whether the known sixteen-element obstruction is a member of a finite list, and enumerating that list in full.
why: A solution would clarify the structural boundary between dyadic, near-regular, and broader quinary matroid behavior.
key_works: Brettell–Pendavingh (2024), [*Computing Excluded Minors for Classes of Matroids Representable over Partial Fields*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13175).

title: Almost all matroids are asymmetric
open: Is a uniformly random labeled matroid on \(n\) elements asymmetric — that is, does its automorphism group become trivial with probability tending to one as \(n\) grows?
status: Conjectured by Mayhew–Newman–Welsh–Whittle. Pendavingh–van der Pol (2019), [*Asymptotics of symmetry in matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04975), showed that almost all matroids are either asymmetric or have automorphism group generated by one transposition, and that almost all sparse paving matroids are asymmetric — leaving exactly the one-transposition case open in general.
solved_when: A proof that the probability a uniformly random labeled matroid on \(n\) elements has trivial automorphism group tends to 1 as \(n \to \infty\).
why: It would justify the expected relationship between labeled and unlabeled enumeration of matroids.
key_works: Pendavingh–van der Pol (2019), [*Asymptotics of symmetry in matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04975).

title: Basis density with a non-prime-power line exclusion
open: For fixed rank \(r\), what is the limiting maximum density \(b(M)/\binom{n}{r}\) of bases among \(n\)-element matroids with no \(U_{2,t+2}\) minor, when \(t\) is not a prime power? The first open case is \(t=6\).
status: The problem is highlighted in Walsh's 2025 problem list, [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666), reporting joint work with van der Pol and Wigal. For prime-power parameters, exact formulas are known and attained by parallel blow-ups of projective geometries.
solved_when: An exact formula (or determined limit) is given for the limiting maximum \(b(M)/\binom{n}{r}\) for fixed rank \(r\), at least for \(t=6\).
why: It isolates the effect of an unavailable finite field on extremal basis counts, since the prime-power cases are governed by projective geometries over existing fields.
key_works: Walsh (2025), [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666), reporting joint work with van der Pol and Wigal.

bib.title: Basis density with a non-prime-power line exclusion

title: Maximum basis density at bounded circumference
open: For each fixed circumference bound \(s\ge4\) and rank \(r\), how densely can bases pack in a matroid with no \(U_{s,s+1}\) minor? Formally, determine the limiting maximum proportion of bases among matroids with all circuits of size at most \(s\).
status: Explicitly open as of 2025. The case of circumference three is settled by an exact formula; for higher circumference, neither matching constructions nor upper bounds are known. See Walsh (2025), [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666).
solved_when: An exact limiting formula for the maximum basis density is obtained for every \(s\ge4\) and fixed rank \(r\), with matching constructions and upper bounds.
why: It quantifies how a purely local circuit-size restriction constrains global independence structure in matroids.
key_works: Walsh (2025), [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666).
